title: Food and Shopping
description: Ten short stories about everyday meals, cooking, stores, markets and paying for food.

lessons.title: Emma Goes to the Store
lessons.summary: Emma buys water, bread and eggs, waits in a long line and pays.
lessons.text:
Emma needs to buy a few things. She needs water, bread and eggs. She has $20. Is that enough money? Emma thinks it is enough.

Emma goes to the store. First, she looks at the water. There is a small bottle and a large bottle. The small one is $1. The large one is $3. Emma wants a lot of water, so she takes the large one.

Then Emma gets the bread. She also gets a few eggs. Now she has the three things. It is time to pay.

There is a long line of people. Emma waits in the line. A man in the line has a small child. They wait too. The line is long, and all the people wait and wait. Emma waits for 10 minutes.

Now Emma can pay. A woman at the store says, "That's $14, please." Emma has enough money. She pays with her $20, and the woman gives her $6 back.

Emma goes home with the water, the bread and the eggs. She still has $6.

Questions:
What does Emma need to buy?
Emma needs to buy water, bread and eggs.
How much money does Emma have?
Emma has $20.
Which water does Emma take?
She takes the large one. It is $3.
What does Emma get after the water?
She gets the bread and a few eggs.
How long does Emma wait in the line?
Emma waits in the line for 10 minutes.
How much does Emma pay?
Emma pays $14.

lessons.title: Dinner for Four
lessons.summary: Tom plans a dinner for four people, and each friend brings one thing.
lessons.text:
Tom has a plan. He wants to make dinner for four people: Tom and three friends. The dinner is at his house, at 7 at night.

Here is the plan. Every person brings one thing. Sara brings bread. Max brings water. Lucy brings a cake. Tom makes the dinner.

Tom starts early. At 3, he is already at work in his house. He works for four hours. At 7, his part is already done.

The friends come at 7. Sara brings the bread. Max brings the water. Lucy brings the cake. Now they have the four things. The plan is working.

The four friends eat and talk until 10 at night. One person talks about work. One person talks about school. One person talks about a game. They talk for three hours.

At 10, every person is full. "I'm full!" says Max. "Me too," says Sara. Lucy and Tom are full too. It is a good night, and it is a good plan.

Questions:
How many people are at the dinner?
Four people are at the dinner: Tom and three friends.
What time do the friends come?
The friends come at 7 at night.
What does each person bring?
Sara brings bread, Max brings water and Lucy brings a cake.
When does Tom start?
Tom starts early, at 3.
How long do the friends eat and talk?
They eat and talk until 10 at night.

lessons.title: The Pizza Order
lessons.summary: Sam orders a pizza by phone, asks the man to say the kinds again, and waits for it.
lessons.text:
Sam is at home, and he wants pizza. He wants to order from a small place called Roma.

Sam calls Roma. A man says, "Hi, this is Roma. Can I take your order?"

"Hi. I want to order a pizza, please," says Sam.

The man has a question. "What kind do you want?"

Sam is not sure. "What kinds do you have?" he asks.

The man says a lot of words, one after the other. Sam doesn't understand them all.

"Can you say that again, please?"

The man says it again, word by word. Now Sam understands every word, and he is sure.

"I want a large cheese pizza, please."

"Do you want anything more?"

"No, I don't want anything more. Thank you."

"Your order comes in 30 minutes."

Sam waits. After 20 minutes, he looks out. Is his order here yet? No, not yet. After 30 minutes, a man from Roma comes with the order. Sam pays, and he says thank you. The pizza is very good.

Questions:
What is the place called?
The place is called Roma.
What question does the man have?
He asks, "What kind do you want?"
Does Sam understand the man the first time?
No. The man says a lot of words, and Sam doesn't understand them all.
What kind of pizza does Sam order?
Sam orders a large cheese pizza.
Is the order there after 20 minutes?
No, it is not there yet.

lessons.title: The Public Market
lessons.summary: Lily walks through the areas of the public market, tries free fruit and pays low prices.
lessons.text:
Lily loves the public market in her city. It is a big place, and it is open to all people. Lily goes there every week.

It has different areas. On the left side, there is a fruit area. On the right side, there is a cheese area.

Lily starts on the left side. Some of the fruit is from her country, and some is from different countries. A man there gives her some for free. "Try it. It's free!" he says. Lily tries it, and it is very good.

Then Lily goes to the right side. A woman there has real cheese from France. It is real French cheese.

The public market has low prices. Lily likes that. Low prices are good for her. She gets fruit and cheese, and she pays only $12.

The market is a long way from her home, though. It is one hour from her house. Lily goes every week, though. She loves it.

Questions:
Where does Lily go every week?
Lily goes to the public market.
What is on the left side?
On the left side, there is a fruit area.
Where is the fruit from?
Some is from her country, and some is from different countries.
What does the man say?
He says, "Try it. It's free!"
How much does Lily pay?
She pays only $12.

lessons.title: A Cake for Anna
lessons.summary: Mia makes a birthday cake with a face on top for her little sister's party.
lessons.text:
Mia is a 12-year-old girl. Her little sister, Anna, turns 6 today. There is a party for Anna at 4. Mia wants to make a cake for the party. She hopes Anna likes it.

At 1, Mia starts. She breaks 4 eggs. She breaks them one by one. Then she adds the other things. The cake needs one hour.

At 2, Mia looks at it. It seems done. It seems good, too.

Then Mia makes a face on the top of the cake. She makes it with fruit. The result is a cake with a big face on top. Mia likes the result. She takes a picture of it and posts it. Her friends like the post.

At 4, the girls come to the party. Anna sees the cake and the face on the top. She turns to Mia. "I love it!" she says. Mia hopes for a good party, and it is a very good party. It is a good day for the two girls.

Questions:
How old does Anna turn today?
Anna turns 6 today.
What does Mia want to make?
She wants to make a cake for the party.
How many eggs does Mia break?
Mia breaks 4 eggs.
What does Mia make on the top of the cake?
She makes a big face.
What does Mia do with the picture?
She posts it.

lessons.title: No Power at Dinner
lessons.summary: The power goes out while Ben is making dinner, so he has bread and cheese until it comes back.
lessons.text:
It is 6 at night. Ben is at home. He is making dinner, and he is watching the food. Then the power goes out. Everything stops. Nothing works.

"What is happening?" Ben thinks. He looks out. The other houses have no power too. Ben goes out, and he sees his friend Jim.

"What is happening?" asks Ben.

"A tree is on the power line," says Jim. "The tree causes the problem. The city is working on it now."

Ben goes back into his house. He has a problem. His dinner is not done, and he can't make it without power. However, he has bread and cheese. He doesn't need power for that. It is a small dinner. However, it is a good one.

Then Ben watches the men from the city. They work for two hours. Nothing happens in the house for two hours. Then the power comes back. Everything works again. The problem is over.

Questions:
What is Ben doing at 6?
He is making dinner, and he is watching the food.
What happens to the power?
The power goes out, and everything stops.
What causes the problem?
A tree on the power line causes the problem.
What does Ben have for dinner?
He has bread and cheese.
When does the power come back?
The power comes back after two hours.

lessons.title: The Family Business
lessons.summary: Leo starts his first job at his family's small food business.
lessons.text:
Rosa and Paul have a small business. They make food, and people come to eat it. Rosa and Paul have two children, Leo and Ana. Every member of the family has a job at the business.

Today is a big day for Leo. He is 16, and today he starts his first job at the business.

At 6 in the morning, the family heads to work. Rosa leads the way. At the business, she leads Leo to the back and shows him his job.

"You take care of the money," Rosa says. "I take care of the food. Paul takes care of the people. Ana takes care of the water."

The work is hard. The day is long. Many people come to eat. Some people come every day. They like to support a small family business. They support Rosa and Paul, and now they support Leo too.

At night, the family heads home. Leo is tired. "This job is hard," he says. "But I like it."

"You work hard," says Rosa. "You are a good member of the team."

Questions:
Who has a small business?
Rosa and Paul have a small business.
What happens today?
Today Leo starts his first job at the business.
Who leads the way?
Rosa leads the way.
What is Leo's job?
Leo takes care of the money.
What do the people like to do?
They like to support a small family business.

lessons.title: Nina's Report
lessons.summary: Nina does a school report about her school's free lunch program.
lessons.text:
Nina is 10. For school, she needs to do a report. Her report is about lunch at her school.

Nina's school has a lunch program. The program provides lunch for every child, and it is free. Every day, it includes water and something good to eat.

First, Nina reads a book about school lunch in different countries. The book has a story about a school in Japan. In the story, the children help to make the food. Nina likes the story.

Then Nina asks the children at her school a question: "Do you ever bring lunch from home?" Some children bring it from home. However, most children get the food from the program. They like it.

Nina does her report. She includes the story from the book. She includes the children's words too. Nina thinks, "My report might be too long. It might not be good."

The next day, Nina's teacher reads the report. "This is a very good report, Nina!" she says.

Questions:
What is Nina's report about?
It is about lunch at her school.
What does the program provide?
The program provides free lunch for every child.
What does it include?
It includes water and something good to eat.
What is the story in the book about?
It is about a school in Japan.
What question does Nina ask?
She asks, "Do you ever bring lunch from home?"

lessons.title: After the Game
lessons.summary: A coach takes his team for pizza after they lose a game.
lessons.text:
Jack is the coach of a small team. The players are 10 years old. Today the team loses the game, 3 to 2. At the end of the game, one player, Ella, misses the ball. She feels very bad.

Jack talks to the players. "We win some games, and we lose some games," he says. "You all play well today. I believe in this team. Ella, I believe in you too."

Then Jack says, "Let me take you all for pizza." Jack drives four players in his car. Ella's dad drives the other players in his car.

On the way, Jack stops and buys a case of water for the team. In the car, Ella holds the case of water. It is big, but she holds it well.

At the pizza place, Jack lets the players order. Every player eats and talks. No player wants to miss a team pizza night.

"Can we do this again?" asks Ella.

"Sure," says Jack. "Win or lose, we always have pizza."

Questions:
Who is Jack?
Jack is the coach of a small team.
Does the team win or lose today?
The team loses the game, 3 to 2.
What does Jack say to the players?
He says, "I believe in this team."
What does Jack buy for the team?
He buys a case of water.
Who holds the case of water?
Ella holds the case of water in the car.

lessons.title: Kate's New Home
lessons.summary: Kate moves to a new city, finds the store close to her home and meets a new friend there.
lessons.text:
Kate moves to a new city. Her new home is a long way away from her old home. She knows no one in the city.

On her first day, Kate needs some things for her home. There is a big store close to her new home, so she goes there.

It has two levels. Things to eat are on the lower level. Things for the house are on the top level.

Kate can't find the milk. She needs someone to help her. She asks someone, "Where is the milk, please?" A woman helps her. "It's on the left side, at the back." The woman's name is Jen, and she lives close to Kate.

Kate gets the milk and more things. She leaves with a bag in each hand. Jen leaves at the same time. "Can I help you?" asks Jen. She takes one bag in her hand, and the two women go home.

At home, Kate puts the bags against the door. "Thank you, Jen," she says. Now Kate has a new friend, and the store is close.

Questions:
Where does Kate move?
Kate moves to a new city, a long way away from her old home.
How many levels does the store have?
It has two levels.
Who helps Kate?
A woman called Jen helps her.
Where does Kate put the bags?
She puts the bags against the door.
